importance_evaluation.scientific_significance: Pioneered fluid mechanics with his formulation of fluid pressure and velocity relationships in Hydrodynamica (1738), provided the earliest kinetic explanation of gas pressure, made fundamental contributions to the theory of vibrating strings, acoustics, and applied probability in epidemiology and economic decision theory.
importance_evaluation.historical_significance: Key figure of the 18th-century Swiss scientific Renaissance and prominent member of the Bernoulli dynasty of mathematicians. He transitioned physics from qualitative mechanical philosophy to rigorous mathematical analysis based on calculus and energy principles.

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Groningen, Dutch Republic, to mathematician Johann Bernoulli.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Recorded in Groningen municipal and church registers (8 February 1700 NS).

timeline_a_biological.event: Completed medical doctorate at the University of Basel with a dissertation on mechanics of respiration.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Basel academic records indicate dissertation thesis defense in 1721.

timeline_a_biological.event: Appointed Professor of Mathematics at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Official appointment records of the Imperial Academy of Sciences in St. Petersburg.

timeline_a_biological.event: Left Saint Petersburg and returned to Basel, assuming the Chair of Anatomy and Botany.
Appointed Chair of Physics at the University of Basel, a position he held until retirement.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: University of Basel faculty appointment records.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Published 'Exercitationes Quaedam Mathematicae' in Venice, solving differential equations and riccati equations.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Published text preserved in major mathematical archives.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Published landmark treatise 'Hydrodynamica' in Strasbourg, establishing conservation of energy in moving fluids and kinetic gas model.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Primary source publication date 1738 (Johann Reinhold Dulssecker, Strasbourg).

timeline_b_scientific.description: Published paper 'Specimen theoriae novae de mensura sortis' in St. Petersburg Academy Commentarii, solving St. Petersburg paradox using expected utility.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Imperialis Petropolitanae Vol. V.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Presented mathematical model evaluating effectiveness of smallpox inoculation to the Paris Academy of Sciences (published 1766).
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences de Paris.

physics_analysis.historical_claim: Formulated relationship between static pressure and flow velocity in flowing fluids based on vis viva conservation.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining mechanical rules governing fluid velocity, head pressure, and discharge through pipes and open orifices.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: Fluid motion conserves vis viva (kinetic energy) while accounting for static head pressure.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Conservation of energy (vis viva) applied to thin slices of incompressible fluid moving along a conduit.
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Bernoulli's equation along a streamline in inviscid, incompressible steady flow: p + 1/2 * rho * v^2 + rho * g * z = constant.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Conducted experiments measuring water flow height in vertical glass tubes attached to pipes of varying diameters.

equations.validity_domain: Inviscid, incompressible, steady-state, non-rotating flow along a single streamline.
equations.assumptions: Zero viscosity, constant fluid density, time-independent flow field.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Foundational principle of fluid dynamics, explaining lift, venturi effect, and pipe flow dynamics.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Fails for turbulent, viscous (boundary layer), or compressible flows without correction terms.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Daniel Bernoulli expressed the relation in terms of hydraulic head and potential/kinetic energy balance. The modern algebraic equation p + 1/2 rho v^2 was explicitly written down later by Leonhard Euler.

physics_analysis.historical_claim: Derived gas pressure from microscopic particle collisions against container walls, yielding Boyle's Law.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Explaining physical origin of gas elasticity and pressure dependence on volume.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: Gas consists of minute particles in rapid random motion; macroscopic pressure results from collisions with container walls.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Section X of Hydrodynamica models gas as cylindrical volume containing moving hard-sphere particles impacting a piston.
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Early version of kinetic theory of ideal gases: P is proportional to particle number density and mean kinetic energy.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Theoretical mechanical derivation verified against Boylean air compression experiments.

equations.assumptions: Point-like non-interacting particles undergo perfectly elastic collisions.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Anticipated modern kinetic theory of gases by over a century before Maxwell and Boltzmann.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Neglected intermolecular forces and energy distribution functions.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Explicitly documented in Section X of Hydrodynamica (1738).

major_claims_audit.claim: Daniel Bernoulli wrote the modern equation p + 1/2 rho v^2 + rho g z = C in Hydrodynamica (1738).
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Daniel Bernoulli formulated the mechanical energy principle for fluids in Hydrodynamica, but the explicit modern differential equation form was developed shortly thereafter by Leonhard Euler.

major_claims_audit.claim: Daniel Bernoulli was the sole founder of modern fluid dynamics.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Daniel Bernoulli laid the experimental and physical energy foundations of hydrodynamics, which Leonhard Euler subsequently developed into continuum field theory equations.

verified_sources.title: Hydrodynamica, sive De viribus et motibus fluidorum commentarii
verified_sources.supported_claim: Formulation of fluid flow energy conservation and kinetic gas model in Section X.

verified_sources.title: Rational Fluid Mechanics 1650–1765 (Editor's introduction to Euler's Opera Omnia)
verified_sources.supported_claim: Historical analysis of Bernoulli's contribution versus Euler's modern formulation of fluid equations.

major_uncertainties: Exact mathematical distinction between Daniel Bernoulli's head-pressure formulation and Euler's continuum pressure gradient fields.
high_risk_claims: Attributing the modern vector-differential form of Bernoulli's equation directly to Daniel Bernoulli without mentioning Euler's contribution.
